title: Memorandum of Commercial Terms: Disruption Credit Rating on Workplace Cafe Management Program Contracts
content:
The commercial terms agreed for a workplace cafe management contract under the Workplace Cafe Management Program provide that the rate a credited meal period earns answers to the claim record standing on the contract.

Where six or more service credit claims have been logged on the contract in the twelve months up to the day the credit is worked out, each credited meal period earns the repeat disruption credit rate. Where three, four or five such claims have been logged over the twelve months up to the day the credit is worked out, each credited meal period earns the recurring disruption credit rate. Where fewer than three such claims have been logged over the twelve months up to the day the credit is worked out, each credited meal period earns the credit rate printed against the service model.

The repeat disruption credit rate is 5.25 per cent. The recurring disruption credit rate is 4.25 per cent. The rate the third band names carries no figure of its own: it is the credit rate printed against the service model in force on the contract.

Claims logged over the twelve months up to the day the credit is worked out, and the rate earned:

| Claims logged | Rate each credited meal period earns |
| --- | --- |
| 6 or more | the repeat disruption credit rate, 5.25 per cent |
| 3, 4 or 5 | the recurring disruption credit rate, 4.25 per cent |
| fewer than 3 | the credit rate printed against the service model |

A claim is counted where a service credit claim has been logged on the contract within those twelve months; it is the logging on the service request log that the count reads, and the window closes on the day the credit is worked out rather than on the day any claim was raised.

Two hypothetical claim records illustrate the bands. A contract hypothetically showing 5 service credit claims logged over those twelve months earns the recurring disruption credit rate of 4.25 per cent on each credited meal period; a sixth claim logged within the same twelve months moves the same contract to the repeat disruption credit rate of 5.25 per cent. A contract hypothetically showing 2 claims logged over those twelve months earns the credit rate printed against its service model.
